title: Tutor CoPilot: A Human-AI Approach for Scaling Real-Time Expertise
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether generative AI can improve real-time instructional support in K-12 tutoring by providing novice tutors with expert-like guidance during live sessions. The central problem is that novice educators often lack the experience to respond effectively in the moment, while traditional professional development is costly, slow to scale, and poorly aligned with immediate classroom or tutoring needs.

The authors introduce Tutor CoPilot, a human-AI system that embeds a language model inside a virtual tutoring platform. When activated during a tutoring session, the tool uses the ongoing conversation, lesson topic, and a selected pedagogical strategy to generate suggestions such as hints, guiding questions, minor corrections, or worked examples. The system was designed using prior work on extracting expert reasoning from think-aloud protocols, and tutors could edit, regenerate, or switch strategies to customize suggestions.

The study was a randomized controlled trial in a live virtual tutoring program with FEV Tutor and a U.S. southern school district. Participants included 900 tutors and 1,800 students from Title I schools, with students in grades 3-8, mostly Hispanic and economically disadvantaged. Tutors were randomly assigned to receive access to Tutor CoPilot or serve as controls. The study lasted two months and focused on math tutoring. Quantitative analyses showed that access to Tutor CoPilot increased exit-ticket mastery, especially for students supported by lower-rated or less-experienced tutors, and improved the language tutors used toward more constructive, understanding-oriented strategies. Tutor interviews suggested the system was helpful but sometimes produced suggestions that were not well aligned to grade level.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a preregistered randomized controlled trial with tutor-level random assignment, a large real-world sample, balance checks, and clustered regression analyses. It also triangulates effects with behavioral message data and reports nulls for some secondary outcomes, which strengthens credibility.
impact_tier_rationale: The main academic outcome is a statistically significant 4 percentage point increase in exit-ticket mastery, with larger gains for lower-rated tutors (9 points), which is a medium-sized practical impact for a priority K-12 population. The intervention is low-cost and directly embedded in authentic tutoring practice, increasing its potential real-world value.

interventions.use_case: Human-AI tutoring support tool that generates real-time, expert-like pedagogical suggestions for K-12 math tutors during live tutoring sessions, including hints, guiding questions, worked examples, and strategy options.

finding.finding_summary: Tutor CoPilot improved proximal math learning outcomes in a preregistered RCT with 782 tutors and 4,136 tutoring sessions. Students whose tutors had access to the system were 4 percentage points more likely to pass exit tickets (62% to 66%, p<0.01), and the conditional pass rate increased by 3 percentage points among students who attempted the ticket (p<0.01).
finding.measure: Math exit ticket pass rate (unconditional and conditional on attempt)
finding.study_size: n=4136 sessions; 782 tutors at launch; 1800 students mentioned in abstract

finding.finding_summary: The intervention had larger effects for lower-performing tutors, indicating greater gains for students taught by tutors who started less effective. Lower-rated tutors’ students were 9 percentage points more likely to pass exit tickets (56% to 65%), and lower-experience tutors’ students were 7 percentage points more likely to pass (61% to 68%).
finding.measure: Math exit ticket pass rate by tutor quality rating and tutoring experience

finding.finding_summary: Tutor CoPilot changed tutor instructional behavior in ways consistent with stronger pedagogical reasoning and student thinking. Treatment tutors were about 2 standard deviations more likely to use strategies such as prompting students to explain and asking questions to guide thinking, and less likely to give away answers or solution strategies.
finding.measure: NLP-classified pedagogical strategy use in tutor chat messages (high-quality vs low-quality strategies)
finding.effect_size: approximately 2 standard deviations on a log-odds scale for some strategy categories

finding.finding_summary: Student self-report survey outcomes did not show statistically significant improvements. Measures including perceived tutor care, confidence in learning math when it is hard, and rating the session or tutor were near zero and non-significant, with treatment effects ranging roughly from -0.004 to 0.03.
finding.measure: Student post-session survey items on tutor care, learning confidence, session rating, and tutor rating
